ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the side length of square $ABCD$ is $2$. Diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$, and $E$ is a point on the extension line of $AC$, with $OE = 2CO$. What is the length of $BE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square, \\
$\therefore AC\perp BD$, $AO=BO=CO=DO$, \\
Since the side length of square $ABCD$ is 4, \\
$\therefore BC=2$, \\
In $\triangle BOC$ (right-angled triangle), \\
$BO^{2}+CO^{2}=BC^{2}$, \\
which means $2CO^{2}=2^{2}$, \\
solving this gives $CO=\sqrt{2}$, \\
Since $OE=2CO$, \\
$\therefore OE=2\sqrt{2}$, \\
In $\triangle BOE$ (right-angled triangle), \\
$BE=\sqrt{OE^{2}+BO^{2}}=\sqrt{(2\sqrt{2})^{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2}}=\boxed{\sqrt{10}}$.
